title: Tensor flatness of the closed-support quotient sheaf
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose open complement $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], set
$$Q^	au_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad 	au=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^	au_{T,C}$. For both topologies, $Q^	au_{T,C}$ is flat: tensoring with it preserves short exact sequences [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Its complex concentrated in degree zero is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. In the etale topology its geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is canonically $A$ on $C$ and zero on $T\setminus C$, with the quotient generator mapping to $1$ on $C$. For $
u_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the canonical comparison $
u_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}\cong Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$ is the one taking $
u_T^*r^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ to $r^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$.

proof.text: Compute the etale quotient stalk directly from its defining cokernel. On C the extension-by-zero source has zero stalk by lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks; preservation of cokernels makes the stalk of the quotient map invertible. Off C, factor the geometric point through the open complement. Restriction of the open counit is an isomorphism by full faithfulness of extension by zero, and the pullback/stalk isomorphism therefore makes the defining arrow invertible on that stalk; its cokernel is zero. For the normalization on C, the point fiber of the constant presheaf is its coefficient module and the point fiber inverts the sheafification unit. Their composite is exactly the constant-section germ in the statement. Compose its isomorphism with the stalk quotient-map isomorphism and take the inverse; the required generator equation is the inverse identity.

source.place: support quotient stalks; the source-library open-extension stalk and point-fiber APIs

proof.text: By lem-sfb-etale-flat-geometric-fibers, the etale quotient is flat as a fixed-scalar module-valued sheaf: its stalks are either zero or the rank-one module, both flat. Transfer this to the canonical etale realization of lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat. Given a finite relation over the constant commutative ring sheaf, intersect the covering sieves on which its finitely many coefficients lift to constant scalars. The scalar action in the realization agrees with the original action, by linearity of module sheafification and the canonical constantModuleHomRingIso. Apply lem-sf-fixed-coefficient-flat-local-relations to the restricted constant-scalar relation. Map the factorization matrix back into the constant ring sheaf. Its section equation follows by linearity, and its zero coefficient equation by naturality and preservation of finite sums and products by the scalar map. Covering transitivity gives the local equational criterion, so lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion-universes gives IsFlatOnSite. This includes empty relations and zero rings.

proof.text: The existing supportQuotientConstantComparison is an isomorphism: compose the constant-sheaf and comparison adjunctions, identify their common right adjoint (global sections at the final object), and use uniqueness of left adjoints. Applying the two Hom equivalences identifies its hom with the exact map in the statement. The canonical comparison for open extension by zero and the restriction comparison are isomorphisms. Apply the unit identity of lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization at the restriction of the constant sheaf; naturality of the restriction comparison and the open-adjunction triangle identity give the commuting square for the two counits. Follow its codomain map by the preceding constant comparison, and its domain map by the image of the restriction of that comparison. Naturality of the pro-etale counit gives a commuting square whose two vertical maps are isomorphisms. The comparison inverse image is a left adjoint and preserves cokernels, so PreservesCokernel.iso followed by cokernel.mapIso gives the required quotient isomorphism and the exact quotient-map identity. The pulled-back quotient map is epic; cancel it to prove uniqueness of the hom and then of the isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat to the fixed-scalar etale quotient and transport flatness across the quotient comparison isomorphism from the preceding step. The coefficient ring is finite and therefore Noetherian. Then lem-sf-intrinsic-realization-flat gives IsFlatOnSite of the specified pro-etale intrinsic realization. For each of the two realized quotient sheaves, its degree-zero single complex is strictly bounded above by zero. Its degree-zero term is the flat sheaf already proved flat; every other term is zero and hence flat; the siteSheafTensorRightIso of lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits identifies the exact monoidal tensor functor with the explicit site tensor functor used by IsFlatOnSite. Apply lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat to obtain precisely IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients. Combine these clauses with the stalk and unique-comparison clauses. No quasi-compactness beyond the unchanged statement is introduced; the direct stalk/comparison route does not need to use that assumption.
